label: sec:planck-scale-computation
html:
Every Planck-time step corresponds to the application of a single transfer matrix on the brane fibre. The product of matrices along the braid word determines the computational cost. The entropy per step equals the operational entropy \eta_q of the substrate.

We realize universal classical computation through a Toffoli transfer matrix on \Sigma_3, yielding an explicit q-AND amplitude that vanishes in the classical limit. The binding of this gate remains robust under noise via linear-program stability. Evaluated as a discrete dynamical system, this constitutes a q-deformed Game of Life. Because the combinatorics is medium-independent, every Turing machine of N gates encodes as a braid with c = 3N crossings. Each Planck step applies exactly one such matrix, with the bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q) bounding the information-theoretic cost.
